## ✨ Highlights

- 🖥️ **The Controller creates its own nodes** on libvirt/KVM hosts: the virtual machine, its image, its network. The node is admitted without approval, and from the page you can power it, open its console, or destroy it. The Controller only ever acts on the virtual machines it created.
- 🧱 **Janus nodes as code**: a Terraform / OpenTofu provider tells the Controller which nodes to have, and changes them in place (network, size, version, extensions).
- 🔑 **API tokens**, for programs - the provider, your scripts - to use the Controller's API.

## 🖥️ Hypervisors

A new **Hypervisors** tab on the Controller.

- **Adding a host**, in three steps:
  1. authorize the Controller's own SSH key for a dedicated account;
  2. read the host key the host presents, and compare it with the host's own;
  3. trust it.

  The card then shows the host's software, CPU, memory, storage pool and networks. Preparing the host - the account, the pool, a polkit policy so that libvirt itself only lets the Controller see and touch its own machines - is in [hypervisors.md](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/docs/hypervisors.md).
- **Creating a node**: name, vCPUs, memory, network interfaces (each on one of the host's allowed networks, static, DHCP or up without an address, matched by MAC address), DNS and NTP. Then either:
  - the Janus version and extensions - the image factory builds the image when the node has extensions;
  - or an image of your own, by URL and SHA-256.

  The image is checked before it reaches the host - the SHA-256 GitHub or the image factory gives - then kept on the host for the next node.
- **Admitted on its token**: the node boots with a one-time registration token, and the Controller admits it as soon as it registers - creating it was the approval. Every other registration still waits for yours.
- **Running it**, from the machine's card or its node's:
  - **Start**, **Force off** and **Reset**, for a node that doesn't answer;
  - its **serial console** in the browser, read-only - private keys hidden: a node prints its admin credential on its first boot;
  - **Destroy**: the node shuts down cleanly first, then its virtual machine and disks are deleted.
- **Changing it in place**, through the API or Terraform:
  - the network, on trial then confirmed;
  - vCPUs and memory: a clean stop, then a restart;
  - the version and extensions: the node's own A/B update, its signature checked, confirmed healthy.

## 🧱 Terraform and OpenTofu

The `swenske/janus` provider: `janus_hypervisor` (trusted on the host key fingerprint you give) and `janus_node`.
- **In place**: network, size, version and extensions change without replacing the node.
- **A new node**: a new name, hypervisor, image or set of interfaces.
- **Import** a node by its ID.

It isn't on the registries yet: build it with `make terraform-provider-build`, and point Terraform at it with a development override - [terraform.md](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/docs/terraform.md).

## 🔑 API tokens

A new **API tokens** tab:
- a token is named, shown once (only its fingerprint is kept), valid for a chosen time or until revoked;
- each token's last use is shown;
- send it as `Authorization: Bearer`;
- it has your rights over the API, except managing tokens;
- a wrong one counts against the same limit as a wrong password.

## 🧩 Nodes

- A node created from this release on presents its registration token: the Controller that created it admits it directly. A node from an older image registers like any other and waits for approval - approving it links it to the machine it runs in.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Controller**: update it from its page.
  - **Nothing to configure**: hypervisors are only there if you add one.
  - **Backups**: its data directory now also holds `hypervisors/` (each one's SSH key), `machines/`, `api-tokens.json` and `controller-id`. Back all of these up with the rest.
- **Nodes**: nothing changes for nodes the Controller didn't create.
